medicinal_chemistry_rationale: CNS-penetrant drug space generally favors MW < 450; 435.5 g/mol is fully compliant.
cLogP = 3.80 falls within the optimal window for passive blood-brain barrier diffusion.
TPSA of 104.7 Å² complies with general CNS guidelines (<120 Å²), though slightly higher than ideal (<90 Å²).
Single donor (-NH2 of oxazoline) minimizes desolvation penalty across lipid bilayers.
8 acceptors passes Lipinski Ro5 (<=10), slightly above conservative CNS guidelines (<=7).
Only 3 rotatable bonds confers high structural rigidity and low entropic barrier upon binding.
QED = 0.624 demonstrates balanced physicochemical properties typical of clinical-stage candidates.
Devoid of pan-assay interference motifs, quinones, rhodanines, or redox cyclers.
No mutagenic, carcinogenic, or metabolically toxic substructures identified.

Flags the amino-oxazoline core [CX3;H0](=N). In medicinal chemistry, this is NOT an unstable aliphatic imine, but rather a cyclic amidine/isothiourea bioisostere that forms the essential hydrogen-bonding network with catalytic aspartates Asp32 and Asp228 (identical to verubecestat).
Mono-fluorination on the solvent-exposed pyrimidine ring elevates lipophilicity (+0.14 cLogP) and blocks oxidative metabolism without disrupting the catalytic binding anchor.
